stories.name: Laguna Pueblo
stories.text: Straight ahead, about 10 miles: Laguna Pueblo. Laguna Pueblo is the home of the Laguna people in west-central New Mexico. Its mission church, San José de la Laguna, was built between 1699 and 1701. That's the story.

stories.name: Mount Taylor
stories.spatialCue: ahead on your right, about 10 miles
stories.text: Ahead on your right, about 10 miles: Mount Taylor. Mount Taylor is a stratovolcano in northwestern New Mexico. Its summit rises to 11,305 feet (3,446 metres). That's the story.

stories.name: Grants
stories.text: Straight ahead, about 10 miles: Grants. Grants is the county seat of Cibola County, New Mexico. Paddy Martinez, a Navajo shepherd, discovered uranium ore near Haystack Mesa, sparking a mining boom that lasted until the 1980s. That's the story.

stories.name: Continental Divide (Campbell Pass)
stories.text: Straight ahead, about 10 miles: Continental Divide (Campbell Pass). Along Interstate 40 east of Gallup, the highway crosses the Continental Divide of the Americas at Campbell Pass. The nearby community sits at about 7,228 feet (2,203 metres). Campbell Pass is a low point along the Continental Divide. That's the story.

stories.name: Gallup
stories.text: Straight ahead, about 10 miles: Gallup. Gallup is the county seat of McKinley County, New Mexico. Historic U.S. Route 66 runs through the center of town, while Interstate 40 passes along its north side. It was founded in 1881. It connects with Grants, which we passed earlier. That's the story.
